title: Training record — objective evidence that somebody learned, not that they can do
description:
What completing a training module produces. It is deliberately NOT a credential, and `attestsCompetence` is const false so it cannot be made into one.

The distinction is the project's founding objection. 'Completed Advanced Metrology Training' is the claim this system exists to replace, and a training layer that quietly issued competence claims would rebuild the problem inside the solution. A training record says one thing honestly: this person did this work on this date.

WHY IT MAY BE SELF-ATTESTED, WHEN A CREDENTIAL MAY NOT. Completing a module is a fact about participation. Demonstrating competence is a claim about ability, and claims about ability need somebody else to stand behind them — hence no self-signoff anywhere on a credential. Applying that rigour here would gate learning behind a witness, which punishes exactly the person with no employer and no professional network. So training records may be self-attested, and they carry correspondingly little weight, and both of those facts are visible.

THE USEFUL PART IS `pending-demonstration`. A skill element cannot be finished by simulation, and the requirement to perform the work on real equipment is not a barrier the system should be trying to dissolve. This state records position precisely: the knowledge is done, the demonstration is not. A mentor or a laboratory reading it knows exactly what is being asked for, and the holder is never left believing the training finished the job.

moduleRef.description: Hash of the module as it stood when completed. Same reasoning as `definitionRef` on a credential: an append-only ID keeps `MOD-0001` resolving, and only a content pin keeps it MEANING what it meant. A module rewritten in 2030 does not retrospectively change what somebody did in 2027.

attestsCompetence.description: Cannot be authored otherwise. A training record is evidence of training and never of competence, however much a holder, an employer or a training provider might prefer otherwise.

attestation.description: Who says the module was completed. Absent means self-attested, which is legitimate here and weak, and a reader should treat it accordingly.

role.description: `trainer` is the metrology-trainer role, whose authority is explicitly to attest completion of training and explicitly NOT to attest competence.

preparedFor.description: The assessable units this module prepared the person for, and where each now stands. Never an attainment — the credential is the only thing that attests attainment.

state.description: `prepared` — the person has done the training and may sit the assessment. `pending-demonstration` — this is a skill element, the training is done, and witnessed performance on real equipment has not happened. Why it has not happened is not recorded and is not the system's business: equipment may be unavailable, or simply not yet used. The state asserts one thing only, which is that preparation is not attainment.

evidence.description: Anything the module produced that is worth keeping — a completed worked example, a simulation transcript. Hashed like any other artifact so it can be looked at again.
